newsitem.title: UK: UK engineering turnover rose 0.4% 3mths to May.
newsitem.headline: UK engineering turnover rose 0.4% 3mths to May.

text.p: Total turnover of Britain's engineering industries rose by 0.4 percent in the three months to May compared with the previous three months, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday.

This was due to an increase of 2.0 percent in export turnover more than offsetting a decrease of 0.8 percent in home turnover. Compared with the same period a year ago, total turnover decreased by 0.2 percent.
Total orders on hand at the end of May fell by 1.3 percent compared to the end of February and were 3.9 percent lower than in May 1996.
Export orders on hand have fallen 7.9 percent from May last year while home orders fell by 1.1 percent. The ONS said new orders coming through were significantly lower than in previous months.
Manufacturers of machinery and equipment suffered a 1.1 percent fall in turnover over the past three months as a 2.8 percent fall in export turnover was not compensated for by flat home turnover.
Total orders on hand were 4.7 percent lower than at the end of February and 3.7 percent down on May 1996.
The ONS said home orders for machinery and equipment were up 1.1 percent compared to a year ago while export orders on hand dropped by 11.3 percent.
For manufacturers of electrical and optical equipment, turnover rose by 1.1 percent over the three months to May as export turnover jumped by 3.9 percent and home turnover slid by 1.2 percent.

Total orders on hand were 1.3 percent up on February but 4.1 percent down on May 1996. Compared to May last year, home orders on hand have dropped by 2.8 percent and export orders have tumbled by 5.7 percent.
